description: Hello, I am Manika, leader of Team Manika's Universe and I am working on the challenge Create health monitoring software for astronauts
summary:
BIO-ASTRA is a low-cost, solar-powered health and environment monitoring system designed for astronauts on long space missions.
We designed it for the challenge to create a health monitoring software for astronauts. Living in space is difficult - gravity, temperature and health risks change every day. Our design monitors astronaut heart rate and cabin temperature, and automatically adjusts cooling, lighting and ventilation to keep the cabin in NASA's comfort range of 21-23°C.
It uses a simple Green / Yellow / Red triage system. Green means normal, Yellow auto-starts the cooling fan, and Red sends an alert to the crew. Inspired by NASA's ECLSS, it is modular, easy to repair, and can be prototyped for around ₹5,000 (∼$60 USD). The same system can also work as a low-cost spin-off for rural PHCs on Earth.
details:
My project bio astra that has the following features. It has several features useful to make astronauts journey happy and comfortable. It's features are as follows:

It uses a Green / Yellow / Red triage system. In Green (60-80 bpm), it maintains normal ventilation. In Yellow (81-100 bpm), it automatically turns on the cooling fan and dims lights to reduce stress. In Red (above 100 bpm), it triggers a visual alert for the crew and flight surgeon. It is inspired by NASA's ECLSS project and targets the NASA comfort range of 21-23°C. It is powered by a 12V solar-charged battery for off-grid habitat use. The design is conceptual and simulated, with a target prototype cost of ₹5,000 (∼$60 USD). I used NASA ECLSS resources as the base of my design, and I used Gemini for designing layouts and documentation. The design is simple, modular, and easy to repair during long missions. Creative dual-use: The same low-cost, solar-powered closed-loop system designed for space can also work as a spin-off in rural PHCs on Earth, where power and medical staff are limited.
